Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Node preemption causing failed transactions - request for SLA credit

Hi Sofia,

We saw a spike of failed payment submissions between 2027-04-29T23:02:00Z and 2027-04-29T23:18:00Z (US-West + us-east routing). Our checkout logs show 1.9% of requests returned 503s; our retries caused duplicate charges for ~12 customers.

StantonPay relies on your low-latency routing; the timing lines up with a reported host preemption event in the traces you provided earlier. Can you confirm the downtime window, the root cause (node preemption vs. internal throttling), and whether StantonPay is eligible for an SLA credit? We need the confirmation and an ETA for a postmortem to share with our execs.

I've attached a short snapshot of our error counts and a few request IDs. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Platform Ops
StantonPay

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 20:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Node preemption causing failed transactions - preliminary traces attached

Hi all,

Preliminary findings: during the 2027-04-29T23:02:00Z window we observed a three-minute host preemption sequence on a small subset of GRPC routers in us-west that briefly exceeded our warm-pool capacity, which caused < 0.5% of requests to be queued and some to return 503 before retrying to healthy backends. At ~23:08Z automatic rebalancing routed traffic to warm instances in us-east.

Attachments included: redwood-trace-logs-04-29.zip (includes request-level traces and host-event notes), edge-node-events-04-29.log (host preemption events). The traces show that for the affected request IDs retries were attempted — a subset saw visible 503s at the client.

Impact summary (prelim):
- Affected window (first evidence): 2027-04-29T23:02:17Z
- Full recovery observed: 2027-04-29T23:11:40Z
- Total global error-rate uplift: ~0.6% (higher for that tenant due to routing distribution)

We are still pulling kernel-level eviction metrics and will include an expanded timeline in the postmortem.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-trace-logs-04-29.zip, edge-node-events-04-29.log

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stantonpay.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Node preemption causing failed transactions - SLA eligibility and compensation proposal

Thanks Karthik — that matches the timeline I was expecting after a quick pass on the traces.

SLA eligibility note: per StantonPay's contract (SLA v2.1) non-excluded availability windows caused by host preemption count toward downtime. Given the recovered window (23:02:17Z–23:11:40Z) and the tenant-level error-rate, I recommend offering a pro-rata credit. Proposed band: 5–10% of the affected day's usage for this account, subject to legal sign-off. If legal requests a tighter calc we can produce a token-level minute-by-minute aggregation; that will take ~48 hours to reconcile fully.

Next steps:
- Legal/finance review credit band (Vanessa) — target: 24–48 hours.
- Postmortem draft: infra to own technical RCAs, SRE to publish a customer-facing summary within 72 hours (Karthik).
- Offer a one-time operational credit and a goodwill gesture (free warm-pool increase for next 30 days) while we implement increased warm-pool thresholds.

Vanessa — please advise on formal credit wording and whether DocuSign is required for settlement. Liam — would StantonPay accept a pro-rated usage credit plus the warm-pool uplift while we finalize?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo-eligibility-summary.pdf

Subject: Re: Node preemption causing failed transactions - SLA adjudication & next steps

Hi Liam,

Thanks for your patience. Quick summary and next steps:

1) Impact window (prelim confirmed): 2027-04-29T23:02:17Z — 2027-04-29T23:11:40Z. Karthik's traces indicate host preemption on a subset of routers caused a temporary shortfall in warm capacity.

2) SLA credit: Rishi proposes a pro-rata credit in the 5–10% range for the affected day; Vanessa will confirm exact amount and formal wording. We can issue the credit to StantonPay’s account once legal approves; no DocuSign required for standard credits.

3) Postmortem & timeline: SRE will publish a customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours. We’ll share the internal RCA and the mitigations we plan (warm-pool thresholds, preemption-resistant routing heuristics).

4) Remediation offer: a complimentary 30-day warm-pool increase for StantonPay and a follow-up call with infra to review mitigations.

I’ve uploaded the preliminary trace bundle and the short impact summary to the Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink. Please let me know whether StantonPay accepts the proposed credit band and the warm-pool uplift; I’ll coordinate the formal credit and postmortem delivery schedule.

If you want a 30-minute call to walk through the traces tomorrow, Rishi and Karthik are available.

Best regards,
